method_summary: A vectorised photon MC (call 013, 3M histories, 15 scoring depths) scores scattered fluence, spectra and angles with an expected-track-length (next-event-to-volume) estimator from every scatter point. Primary fluence comes from the same ray-attenuation estimator integrated over 3M source rays (call 014). L2 and L3 come from folding the MC fluence spectra with cross sections and KN samples (calls 016-017). L4 comes from a CSDA slowing-down spectrum with iterated Moller deltas (call 020), and the L4 angular distribution from a small condensed-history electron MC (call 025). notable_physics_choices: Scoring is a volume next-event estimator: from the source and each scatter site it adds the attenuated expected track length exp(-mu*s)(1-exp(-mu*L))/mu in the cylinder, not analog track length. Rayleigh angles use the Thomson (1+cos^2)/2 shape with no form factor. The photoelectric coefficient is the residual mu_tot-mu_KN-mu_coh-mu_pair, which gives a spurious ~0.6% photoelectric share for primary photons. Annihilation photon directions are sampled with theta uniform in [0,pi], which is not isotropic. There is no photon energy cutoff. g is effectively assumed through mu_tr=mu_en*1.0055 (so g=0.0055 and K follow from that factor). PDD5=80.6% is a collision-kerma ratio Kcol(5)/Kcol(0.5) with no build-up; call 028 hard-codes the 80.61 taken from the call-027 output. The L4 angular MC (call 025) uses Highland multiple scattering in an infinite medium, seeded from the binned L3 directions.
